To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of the MSGC detector with neon-xeon gas mixture is inferior to the performance of the same detector with pure xenon and the performance of the detector with argon-xeon gas mixtures.

neon-xenon mixture fillings are inferior to argon-xenenon mixtures in terms of detector performance, but the detector gain and energy resolution can be improved by about 50% with neon-xenen mixtures as compared to pure xenon.

the performance of the GPSP/MSGC hybrid is limited by optical feedback in all gas mixtures investigated, that the best performance is achieved with argon/xenon mixtures, that the best energy resolution is achieved for positive feedback gain in the range 1.1-1.2, and that the best resolution is achieved for xenon content of 50-80%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new gas mixtures for the application of gas proportional scintillators in x-ray spectrometers.

the development of a high-resolution, high-efficiency and high-rate-capable hybrid detector based on the use of a microstrip plate as a scintillation detector in direct contact with a proportional scintillation counter.
the optimization of the detector design and gas mixtures to obtain the highest detector gains and the best x-ray energy resolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of neon-xenenon mixtures for x-ray spectroscopy with proportional scintillation counter detectors using a CsI coated MSP is not recommended.

the neon-xenon mixture is not a promising candidate as an alternative to pure xenon or argon-xenom mixtures for the application as gas-fillings for x-ray spectrometer detectors based on a hybrid design of a proportional gas counter and a CsI-coating on a microstrip plate.
the performance of the GP/SC hybrid detector is not improved for neon-xenon filling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the performance of the GP/MSGC detector with argon-xe mixtures is superior to that achieved with Ne-Xe mixtures, and the performance achieved with Ne-Xenon mixtures can be improved by using a CsI coating with a higher CsI content.
the use of neon-xen-on gas mixture is not recommended for the application as a VUV-photosensor for the GPSC/ MSGC hybrid detectors for x-ray spectroscopy.
neon-xenon and argon- xenon mixtures are not suitable for x-ray spectrometer applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of neon as an additive in the scintillation mixture of a xenon-filled detector does not result in an improvement of the detector performance.
the performance of a hybrid MSGC/GPS detector is limited by the optical feedback and not by the scintillation yield.
neon-xenon mixture is not a suitable alternative to argon-xen on mixture for x-ray spectrometer applications with the GPSC/MS P detector configuration.
